passage:
Archaeologists found an ancient trash pit. It contained broken pottery, fish bones, seeds, and burned wood.
Students thought trash sounded unimportant. The guide explained that trash can reveal what people ate, made, traded, and threw away.
The class then studied their own school trash for one day, wearing gloves and recording categories. They found food waste, plastic wrappers, paper, and many unfinished drinks.
They realized future historians could learn about them from what they wasted.
Trash is embarrassing because it shows habits without politeness. That is why it can be honest evidence. What people throw away tells a story.
